title: Adjoint mates on cartesian derived sections
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with a fixed compactification $f=pj$. For $W=X,Y$ let $\mathscr S_W$ be the abelian category of strict semilinear systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves on the small pro-etale site: an object has maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_{n+1}\to A_n}M_n$, and morphisms commute with these maps. Use its ordinary unbounded derived category and its exact evaluations $e_n$. Let $\mathscr N_W$ be the full subcategory of normalized systems, meaning that every transition-adjoint $t^M_{m,n}:M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to M_n$ is invertible, whose individual levels lie in $D^b_{ctf}(W,A_n)$. No uniform cohomological or Tor interval is imposed in this notation.

The ordinary system compact-support functor $\mathcal F_f=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ restricts to $\mathscr N_X\to\mathscr N_Y$. It has a right adjoint $\mathcal E_f:\mathscr N_Y\to\mathscr N_X$, constructed from a right adjoint on the ambient derived category of strict etale systems and etale/pro-etale comparison; existence of $\mathcal E_f$ is a conclusion. There are specified natural identifications
$$e_n\mathcal F_f\cong F_n e_n,\qquad e_n\mathcal E_f\cong G_n e_n,$$
where $F_n=Rf_{!,A_n}$ and $G_n=Rf^!_{A_n}$ are the finite constructible adjoints, with their specified units $\eta_n$ and counits $\epsilon_n$. These identifications preserve the counits, hence the units. If $T^W_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ and $q_{m,n}:T^Y_{m,n}F_m\xrightarrow{\sim}F_nT^X_{m,n}$ is the canonical compact-support comparison, the reduction transitions are
$$t^{\mathcal F_fM}_{m,n}=F_n(t^M_{m,n})q_{m,n,M_m},\qquad t^{\mathcal E_fN}_{m,n}=G_n(t^N_{m,n})b_{m,n,N_m},$$
where $b_{m,n}$ is the $F_n\dashv G_n$ transpose of $T^Y_{m,n}(\epsilon_m)q_{m,n,G_m}^{-1}$. It is the canonical invertible finite comparison of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. The unit and counit are actual morphisms of ordinary derived systems and satisfy the triangle identities there.

For $M\in\mathscr N_X$, $N\in\mathscr N_Y$, use the fiberwise mapping systems $\mathcal H_W$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. There is a specified natural isomorphism
$$\Phi_{M,N}:\mathcal H_Y(\mathcal F_fM,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H_X(M,\mathcal E_fN)\quad\text{in }D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab})).$$
It is constructed by the ordinary system tensor-Hom adjunction, the compact-support projection formula and the actual system counit. Its evaluation is the finite derived mapping-complex adjunction; on degree-zero Hom its maps are $h\mapsto\mathcal E_f(h)\eta_M$ and $g\mapsto\epsilon_N\mathcal F_f(g)$. Applying $R\lim$ gives an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$. Units, counits, evaluation transposes and inverse identities are specified before taking $R\lim$. The construction respects ordinary mates of specified transformations of the actual system compact-support functors, in particular geometric composition comparisons. Tensor-evaluation and tensor-Hom transposes built from these actual maps and derived system tensors are system maps with the corresponding finite evaluations.

proof.text: Use the existing finiteAdjunctionDiagramRealization theorem to obtain the actual normalized realization r, geometry, sections comparison, signed symmetries and Enriched structure. Discard its additional dualizing and coherence witnesses.

Apply normalizedSupportEtalePresentation to r.support, r.F and r.supportIso. Compare the resulting normalized right adjoint H with r.G by r.adjunction.rightAdjointUniq. Whiskering this isomorphism with the inclusion gives rightComparison. Naturality and unit_rightAdjointUniq_hom_app identify the two Hom bijections; compose with its inverse to obtain exactly EtaleOrigin.transpose.

Prove MateEvaluation directly: apply injectivity of the finite inverse Hom equivalence, precompose with the invertible support-evaluation comparison, and use its naturality and r.counit. The ordinary conjugateEquiv_counit identity turns the system mate into the given transformation followed by the other counit. Substitute the two supplied compatibility equations, move the right comparison past the finite transformation by naturality, and apply conjugateEquiv_counit at the finite level. The inverse mate identity is symm_apply_apply.

The finite_exceptional theorem supplies invertibility of every quotient mate b. The adjunction homEquiv_unit and homEquiv_counit identities give both degree-zero formulas. Applying the derived-limit functor to the two inverse identities of Enriched.iso proves both limit inverse equations; functors preserve its isomorphism.

Specialize systemAdjunctionTransposeCoherence to the proetale selector and each W equal to X or Y. The existing coefficient sheaf and transition definitions agree with these selectors. This supplies SystemTensorTransposeCoherence for every requested calculus A.
